title: Attempt-audit assertion does not verify ordering before destructive work
scenario: Move the reset-attempt audit write after the first provider credential deletion but before the second deletion throws. The current assertions still observe one attempt row and one removed factor after the request.
expected: The test verifies a durable attempt row already exists when the first destructive provider call starts.
actual: The provider double only records deleted IDs; the attempt row is queried after reset(target) returns. No assertion is made at the destructive-call boundary.
evidence: Static coverage review at 7e61db71e8a089e52d3bae9ffacdf7022907b2cd: MfaResetAuditIntegrationTest.java:45-50 records deletion only; :95-99 queries audit after failure. Production MfaAdminController.java:100-106 currently has correct ordering. This is a test gap, not an observed production ordering failure. Container test NOT_RUN locally.
suggested_fix: Query audit persistence from the provider double before its first deleteCredential call, preferably through an independent connection/transaction, and assert the target-specific attempt exists. Retain partial-failure assertions.
repro_test: A disposable mutation moving the attempt write after the first delete must fail the strengthened integration test; mutation was not executed locally because the test requires PostgreSQL containers.
